title: The Choir of Cold Spring
premise: Silas Winterbourne, a pest controller who prides herself on never believing in anything she can't trap or poison, is called to the Holloway house in Cold Spring, where something has been leaving wet fingerprints on every window. When photographs of her late grandmother's house begin showing an extra chair at the table, Silas realizes the summons was never about pests—the town invited something into the well decades ago, and it has chosen her as its heir. As the entity's presence spreads through mirrors, hymnals, and the memories of neighbors who insist they've always known her, Silas must decide whether loyalty to Cold Spring's collective silence is worth surrendering her own identity. She survives by refusing to belong: at dawn, with the well refilling, she speaks the truth aloud to the assembled choir of townsfolk, breaking the invitation and drowning the thing's claim on her name—though one photograph still shows an empty chair, waiting.
about_author: Lena Halloran is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper obituary writer who spent years cataloguing the things rural communities refuse to say out loud. She lives near an old reservoir and writes her fiction entirely before sunrise.

chapters.title: Wet Prints on the Glass
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Called to the derelict Holloway house for a 'rat problem,' Silas finds handprints on the inside of sealed windows and a child's chair that no one owns. She treats it as squatters and leaves poison. Emotional beat: professional confidence masking a lifetime of practiced disbelief.

chapters.title: The Extra Chair
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Sorting her grandmother's estate photos, Silas notices a wooden chair appearing in images spanning forty years—including pictures taken after the furniture was sold. Her aunt Maren goes pale and begs her not to ask the town about it. Emotional beat: the first hairline crack in her skepticism.

chapters.title: Hymnal for the Dry Season
chapters.summary: POV Silas. At the Cold Spring church archive, she finds hymnals water-stained from the inside and a 1974 service program titled 'The Welcoming.' Pastor Ede admits the town holds an annual vigil but refuses to say what they welcome. Emotional beat: suspicion curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Everyone Remembers You
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Neighbors greet Silas by a childhood nickname she never had; the diner waitress describes her grandmother teaching her to sing 'to keep it fed.' Maren confesses Silas was promised to the well at birth—a debt the family fled. Emotional beat: identity itself begins to feel borrowed.

chapters.title: What the Well Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Silas. She descends into the capped well behind the Holloway house and finds the missing chair, warm to the touch, ringed by decades of offerings. Something below breathes her name in her grandmother's voice. Emotional beat: terror fused with a horrible homesickness.

chapters.title: The Vigil
chapters.summary: POV alternating Silas and Pastor Ede. The town gathers for the annual Welcoming; Ede's chapters reveal he inherited the duty and hates it. The congregation sings while Silas watches the well water rise without rain. Emotional beat: complicity—she realizes her presence is the offering.

chapters.title: Choir of the Drowned
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Trapped overnight in the church as fog pours in singing in familiar voices, Silas sees the dead of Cold Spring—including her grandmother—standing in the pews, mouths moving in unison. They aren't threatening her; they're begging her to join. Emotional beat: grief weaponized against her.

chapters.title: Maren's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Maren. Flashback chapter: 1998, Maren took baby Silas and ran, trading her own memory of the truth to buy time. Now, aging and forgetting, she returns to pay the debt herself. Emotional beat: love expressed as sacrifice, loyalty as a cage.

chapters.title: Sunrise Clause
chapters.summary: POV Silas. With Maren held at the well's edge and the water rising toward refill, Silas confronts the entity wearing her grandmother's face. It offers belonging—every memory, every name, every place at the table—in exchange for consent. Emotional beat: the temptation of home set against self-erasure.

chapters.title: The Truth Before Refill
chapters.summary: POV Silas. As dawn breaks, Silas speaks the town's buried crime aloud before the assembled choir, naming what was invited in and shattering the consent that sustains it. The well drains; the extra chair vanishes from every photograph except one. Emotional beat: costly liberation—truth saves her, but Cold Spring will never forgive her for surviving.
